fix: Better bearer: 'Calyx ... lobes' could go to calyx lobe (FLOPO_0986005). Sepal is acceptable. 'ovate-elliptic' is a shape between ovate and elliptic, so elliptic is the nearest single term.
reason: The calyx lobes are said to be ovate-elliptic. Sepal + elliptic says that, only a little less exactly.
The base of the minor leaf blade is rounded and decurrent, so leaf lamina base + decurrent is right.

fix: In 'X to X-Y', the range ends at the compound shape X-Y. The hyphen inside 'ovate-lanceolate' was read as its own ovate-to-lanceolate range, and the first 'ovate' was dropped. Read the hyphenated compound as one shape at the end of the 'to' range.
reason: The flora says the outer phyllaries are ovate to ovate-lanceolate, and only the innermost are lanceolate. The relation runs ovate→lanceolate, which makes the outer phyllaries reach fully lanceolate.

target: calyx tube (FLOPO_0986011) longer than calyx lobe (FLOPO_0986005)
fix: In 'Calyx ..., tube longer than lobes', both 'tube' and 'lobes' are parts of the calyx. The bearer should be the calyx tube and the part compared with should be the calyx lobe. The pipeline used the calyx itself and linked 'lobes' to leaf lamina lobe (PO_0025517). Bare 'lobes' must take the organ named in the same sentence.
reason: It is the calyx tube, not the whole calyx, that is longer than the lobes. The comparison target, leaf lamina lobe, is also the wrong organ.
'Thinly textured' leaves are thin leaves, so decreased thickness fits.
Corolla 9–16(–20) mm long: the range and the rare maximum of 20 are recorded correctly.
The corolla is purple or white (white with a bluish tinge). These are true colour alternatives in the flora.

fix: In Carex, 'utricle' means the perigynium (PO_0009044), not the fruit. 'Glume' means the scale under the flower, not the grass spikelet glume (PO_0009039). Use these meanings for Cyperaceae text.
reason: The flora says the utricles (perigynia) are longer than the female scales. The annotation instead puts fruit against a grass glume.

fix: With 'X outside and Y on the inside', the 'outside' slot must be kept. The corolla's outer surface should be the bearer, or the place should be recorded in the context.
reason: Only the outside of the corolla is papillose-pubescent. The inside of the tube is just pubescent, so 'corolla papillose' is too broad.
The leafy shoots are erect. Shoot system + erect is right.
'Anthers without pollen' means pollen is absent, so the negated 'pollen present' is right.

fix: Keep the position word ('lowest', 'upper') when a comparison is said of only one bract in a series.
reason: Only the lowest bract is longer than the inflorescence; the upper bracts are reduced. Without 'lowest', the statement is false for most bracts.
The leaf blade base is cuneate.
'Oppositifoliées' means the flowers (or flower clusters) sit opposite a leaf. This is one of the alternatives the genus description lists.

target: prickle (PO_0025169) on the leaf margin and midrib
fix: Pandanus leaf 'spines' are marginal and midrib prickles or teeth, not thorns (which are modified branches). Map 'spines at margins / on midrib' of leaves to prickle, and keep the leaf as the whole they belong to.
reason: The 1–3 mm length is right, but thorn is the wrong structure for the spines on a Pandanus leaf.
This text describes the calyx (the corolla follows after it). The outside of the calyx is puberulent, so sepal abaxial epidermis + puberulous fits.

fix: In 'apex X to Y' inside a fruit description, the apex is the part that bears the shape. Keep the apex as the bearer (or as a place on the part) instead of dropping it into the whole fruit.
reason: The flora says the apex of the fig is convex to flat, not the whole fig. The fig itself is ellipsoid to obovoid.
1 or 2 flowers at each node of the rachis: the count, the inflorescence as container and the per-node slot are right.
The leaves are sessile or nearly so, which is sessile with the 'approximately' qualifier.
The stem is pubescent or glabrous. The 'fulvous' (tawny) colour of the hairs is not part of this annotation.
The legume is yellowish, so fruit + yellow with 'approximately' is right.

target: subcircular to oblong / subcircular to oblanceolate
fix: 'A to B or C' means a range from A to B, or from A to C. Here the 'to' range was dropped and only 'B or C' was kept as alternatives, which leaves out A.
reason: The blade is subcircular to oblong or oblanceolate. The relation keeps only oblong or oblanceolate and loses subcircular.

fix: 'Mostly adnate', followed by 'free parts ...', says how much of the stipule is joined, not how often. It should not become the frequency qualifier 'usually'.
reason: The stipules are mostly fused to the petiole, with the upper parts free. That is a degree of fusion, not 'usually fused'.

target: glabrous abaxially, hairy only along the midvein and in the axils of the secondary veins
fix: 'Glabrous except for hairs along/in X' means glabrous, with hairs only in place X. Record that place, or annotate glabrous with the exception. Do not record plain 'hairy' on the whole surface.
reason: The lower blade surface is mostly glabrous. 'Hairy' with no place says the opposite of the flora.
The sepals have resin dots, which is gland-dotted. The petals need their own annotation.

fix: In '1-loculed, occasionally 2-loculed', 1 is the usual value and 2 is a rare extreme. Record the range 1–2 with 2 as a rare maximum, or keep the qualifier 'occasionally'. Do not record a plain count of 2.
reason: A plain count of 2 locules turns the rare case into the normal one. The ovary is normally 1-loculed.

fix: In 'the base of the stem X', the bearer is the stem base (PO_0008039), not the stem.
reason: This is a perennial herb, and only the base of its stem is woody.
The leaf has 8–12 leaflets.

target: trichome (hairs) on the stem: colour silvery to ferruginous
fix: In 'with X hairs', a colour word describes the hairs, not the organ that bears them.
reason: The hairs are silvery to ferruginous (rust-brown). Nothing is said about the colour of the stem itself.
'Roots fibrous' means fibrous-rooted, and the constraint file allows root as its bearer.
